dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Ah, the air here is so peaceful and calming.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: If we put on a slow concerto right now, I'm sure the cadenza would be brimming with inspiration.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How do you like it here?

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: You know... it almost feels like coming home. No picky customers, no reputation to uphold... Here, I can cook whatever I feel like. It's a nice chance to try out some new things from my list.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Just to be clear — you are gonna set me up with a purpose-built kitchen here, right?

choices.text: Make yourself at home, why don't ya...

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Hehe~ Don't worry, I'll make sure it's worth your while.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: In Fontaine, I have hundreds of rich and famous people offering handsome sums of Mora on a daily basis, hoping for the chance to add just one exquisite dish to their family feast.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: I don't even have the time to turn them all down. Some of the letters I get go unopened and unread.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: But you, on the other hand — all you need is to provide an oven, a stovetop, a cupboard, and a water source. I've brought all the cooking utensils and ingredients that I need.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: No one else in all of Fontaine, or even all of Teyvat, could hope for the special treatment I'm offering you.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: And all I ask in lieu of a salary... is that you give me a thorough and honest review of each dish once you've had the pleasure of consuming it.

choices.text: But I don't know enough about your cooking methods...

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Oh, don't worry — I trust you, you have good taste. And I have full confidence in our culinary compatibility. So you set up the kitchen however you like. Once I get to work, I'll be right in my element.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: You and I are like Lumidouce Bells and Rainbow Rose foam: one tender and delicate, the other sweet and sour. A perfect combination.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: I know if I cook for you based on gut instinct, you'll like what I come up with.

choices.text: What if my kitchen's not up to your standards?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Would you like to have a chat with me?

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Oh, do I!? You walked right into this one. I've got a lot of questions for you...

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Relax, I'm just curious about you, that's all.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: You're the most widely traveled out of all the people I know. The things you've seen, the battles you've fought... I don't know anyone else whose experience comes close to yours.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Hmm... So, my question is — out of all the food, or maybe... food-adjacent things you've encountered on your travels, is there anything out there that's made you curious about how it might taste?

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Oh, um... Ahem, not that I'm trying to encourage you to just start licking everything you see, of course.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: It's just, I want to challenge myself. See if I can replicate some really obscure or outlandish flavors using substitute ingredients.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Basically, if there's any flavors in the world strange enough to pique your curiosity, then trying to imitate them has gotta be one of the most technically demanding challenges in all of precision gastronomy.

choices.text: I'm not an adventurous eater. I prefer to go with what I know.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Oh, really? Hmm, you surprised me with that answer.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: I suppose curbing your curiosity can be important for self-preservation. It means you avoid the more experimental dishes out there. Not to mention food poisoning...

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: But, I'm still confident that I can create some new and tantalizing flavors to expand your comfort zone...

choices.text: I'm kinda curious about... slimes and specters.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Aha, there it is! The taste of elemental life-forms — a question that has intrigued the culinary world for centuries.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: A lot of people draw associations with fruits and other plants of a similar color. For instance, it's commonly held that Cryo Slimes taste like Mint, and Electro Slimes taste like Wolfhooks...

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: However, the samples of Slime condensate that I've collected myself seem to refute this idea. The compounds that they contain are quite contrary to what you'd expect. Hydro Slimes, for example — you'd think they taste like Sea Ganoderma, but in fact they're completely tasteless...

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: And while Pyro Slimes do have a spiciness akin to the Jueyun Chilis of Liyue, they also contain small amounts of an intensely sweet substance.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: It's decided! I'll recreate the flavor for you the next time we have afternoon tea.

choices.text: If you want a real challenge... how about clockwork meka?

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Metal and raw energy? Huh? Now those sound like some interesting flavors!

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: I actually wondered the same thing when I was a kid. What does White Iron taste like? What about imported Starsilver?

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Unsurprisingly, both tasted absolutely terrible... White Iron tastes like two parts mud, three parts hay, and five parts white wax.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Starsilver actually had notes of snow and ice... but it was like snow and ice mixed with limewash paint. Just a little taste is enough to send you into a coughing fit.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: As for raw energy... I've never been brave enough to try a Pneumousia block or anything like that. If I had to guess, though, I bet it causes a tingling sensation. By virtue of the damage it would do to your tongue.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Recreating that flavor in a dish would be a major challenge... I guess I'd start with crushed ice as a base and go from there. Let's revisit this when the weather gets a bit warmer!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there anything you'd like to do?

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Oh, plenty of things... There's so much I wanna try. It feels kinda greedy of me...

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: I want to learn how to paint. I'd love to have a painter's level of familiarity with the whole color spectrum, so I could explore the interplay between color, emotion, and taste, and apply that knowledge in the kitchen.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: I also wish I could study engineering, so I could tinker around with my two meka... the goal being to handle the work of a whole team of chefs in a fraction of the time.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Bladesmithing is another area I'd love to know more about. If I could custom-build my very own set of kitchen knives, all thirty-three varieties, then I could really fine-tune my ingredient preparation.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Finally, I wish I was a master composer. Then I could write a dedicated piece of music for each dish in my repertoire, and give my customers the ultimate multi-sensory experience when they savor my dishes...

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: You could say I have an insatiable appetite for trying new things, but ultimately it all boils down to one thing — improving my cooking. Everything I've mentioned is in service of that one goal.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: So I guess, wherever my interests might take me, they'll always lead me right back to the kitchen where I started.

choices.text: There's nothing wrong with having one area as your main focus.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Yeah, I know. Realistically speaking, if I wanted to get seriously proficient in any of the things I've mentioned, it'll take decades of hard work and dedication.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: It's the same with cooking. There's much more to being a good chef than being able to follow a recipe. Like any discipline, it gets tough pretty quickly once you get into it. Not for the faint-hearted, that's for sure!

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: In your case, though... I think you might actually be on track to become the kind of multi-disciplinary expert I could only dream of being.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: That's right. I see limitless potential in you... Potential that isn't tied down by a fixed mindset.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Plus, you have the willpower, the good judgment, and the ability to follow through.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: If anyone in this world could hope to master all the skills I mentioned simultaneously, it's you.

choices.text: Thank you for the high praise, Chef...

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: You bet... And once you've mastered everything, come back to me. It'll be your turn to don the head chef's cap and teach me everything you know.

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: I'm predicting that we'll spend days on end at the stove, churning out one show-stopping dish after another, until we've prepped, cooked, and plated half of Teyvat!

response.speaker: Escoffier
response.text: Ahh, I can't wait!

choices.text: You're right. If I work hard at it, I think I should be able to do it.
You see me as a polymath one day?
Spread yourself too thinly, and you might not learn anything at all.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good morning, Escoffier.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Someone's perky this morning... I was gonna make you some breakfast, but it seems like you have more energy than me. Why don't you whip us something up instead?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good night, Escoffier.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Alright, goodnight. I'm gonna wait till you're soundly asleep and then start cooking... Whichever dish smells good enough to coax you out of your dream-state and back to reality, that'll be our main course for tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Mm, very meticulous! Down to the last detail. This is on par with the Hotel Debord. A clean and tasteful dining environment can do a lot to improve people's appetite.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: What's the next step — ambush some big-shot chef and convince them to come cook for you? Hehehe... Wait, hold on... am I the one being ambushed!?

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: ...Alright, deal, suits me anyway. Gimme a call when you're hungry and I'll whip you up a feast.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Look at that, beautiful... It's just like an oil painting. So colorful.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Certain colors evoke particular flavors very strongly. For instance, just a glimpse of the blue-and-green hues of Mint in the distance feels crisp and refreshing, while the glossy orange of Bulle Fruit is intrinsically sharp and sweet.

dialogues.speaker: Escoffier
dialogues.text: Then there's your hair color... Oh, not that I'm gonna gobble you up! I just mean... Up close, you give off a unique, glorious radiance, both visually and in terms of your energy.
